findings.explanation: The Splunk Add-on for Cisco UCS assigns all events sourcetype `cisco:ucs`, with the class in `source` (`cisco:ucs:firmwareRunning`). dataSources, implementation and every detailedImplementation probe search rely on a sourcetype the add-on does not emit. The repository guide has the same error.
findings.quote: sourcetype `cisco:ucs:inventory` from the Splunk Add-on for Cisco UCS
findings.suggested_fix: Use `sourcetype=cisco:ucs source=cisco:ucs:firmwareRunning` and validate with `| stats count by source`.

findings.explanation: The reverse is true. The Splunkbase package name and the add-on's documented paths are `Splunk_TA_cisco-ucs`, so `local/inputs.conf` inside `Splunk_TA_cisco_ucs` targets a non-existent directory. dataSources repeats the same claim.
findings.quote: the legacy hyphenated string `Splunk_TA_cisco-ucs` may still appear in download filenames and in older `app.conf` stanzas but the canonical add-on id is the underscore form
findings.suggested_fix: State that the app directory is `Splunk_TA_cisco-ucs` and fix all paths.

findings.explanation: The add-on is configured with Managers (splunk_ta_cisco_ucs_servers.conf: server_url, account_name), Templates listing classIDs (splunk_ta_cisco_ucs_templates.conf: content), and Inputs binding `servers`, `templates`, `interval`, `index` and `sourcetype`. There is no `ucsm_url` key or inventory toggle.
findings.quote: commonly a modular input whose name is prefixed in the style `cisco_ucs://<descriptive_name>`; copy that pattern into `local/inputs.conf`, set `disabled = 0`, point `ucsm_url` to `https://<ucsm-fqdn>`
findings.suggested_fix: Describe adding a UCSM Manager, a Template whose content includes firmwareRunning, and an Input referencing both at a daily or 3600 s interval.

findings.explanation: BIOS, CIMC and adapter firmware strings are model- and generation-specific (a B200 M5 BIOS string never equals a C240 M7 one). A lookup keyed only on component_type marks every model except one as non-compliant. The text mentions per-domain splits but never per-model ones.
findings.quote: Required columns: `component_type` (one of: `BIOS`, `Adapter`, `StorageController`, `CIMC`, `Other` to match the `case()` in the search), and `approved_version`
findings.suggested_fix: Key the baseline on model (from computeBlade/computeRackUnit `model`) plus component_type, or on the UCSM host firmware package/bundle version, and explain how to join model onto the firmware rows.

findings.explanation: hardware lists X-Series compute nodes as in scope, while exclusions excludes X-Series as Intersight-managed. UCSM 4.3(2a)+ can manage X9508 domains, so the scope rule should be "UCSM-managed or not", not model family. X410c M6 also looks non-existent (X410c shipped as M7).
findings.quote: UCS X210c M6/M7, UCS X410c M6
findings.suggested_fix: Scope by management mode (UCSM 4.3(2a)+ X-Series in scope; IMM out of scope) and correct the X410c generation.

findings.explanation: The scenarios do not apply to a weekly inventory report. Real false positives are mid-wave firmware upgrades with pending activation (startup ≠ running until reboot), PSIRT emergency exceptions, and short versus long version strings. The troubleshooting section touches on these, but this field does not.
findings.quote: Planned work for 'Firmware Compliance (Cisco UCS)' shifts `last_seen` over `span=1h`
findings.suggested_fix: List upgrade-in-progress/pending-reboot, approved exceptions, and version string format mismatches, with their handling.

findings.explanation: Marked verified although the sourcetype and input stanza do not match the add-on documentation.
findings.suggested_fix: Set to draft until validated on a live add-on install.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: The base search requires sourcetype="cisco:ucs:inventory", which the Splunk Add-on for Cisco UCS does not emit (sourcetype cisco:ucs, source cisco:ucs:firmwareRunning), so it returns no events on a default install.
`like(classId, "firmware%")` is an eval function used inside the `search` command, which does not evaluate functions, so that OR branch never matches as intended. Use `where` or `classId=firmware*`.

Lookup on component_type alone with a string equality test cannot express model-specific baselines, so mixed-generation fleets show mass false non-compliance. The `%mgmt%` branch also labels board-controller and other mgmt/fw-system rows as CIMC.

summary: The UC is a well-explained firmwareRunning compliance report with practical validation steps. It inherits the category-wide add-on errors: a non-existent `cisco:ucs:inventory` sourcetype, a reversed app directory name and an invented `cisco_ucs://` input stanza. Its single-version-per-component-type baseline also cannot represent model-specific BIOS/CIMC firmware.
